title: Unique identifier linking
description: Device ID transferred from wearable to companion app can be used as a unique identifier to link data across sessions and potentially across devices.

title: Quasi-identifier combining data
description: Exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps can be combined to identify individuals and link data across different contexts.

title: Profiling an individual
description: The combination of exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps can be analyzed to create profiles of individual users and their activities.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The wearable device processes and transfers identified data (device ID, timestamps) to the companion app.

title: Identifier in data
description: Device ID is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject that is included in the transferred data.

title: Revealing attributes
description: GPS traces and exercise sessions are revealing attributes that can support identification of the data subject.

title: Attributable data evidence
description: Data records can be attributed to a specific user through the device ID, preventing denial of certain claims about activity.

title: Observed communications
description: The data flow from wearable to companion app can be observed by third parties or network monitors.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: GPS traces and exercise sessions are potentially sensitive data types that may be collected beyond functional requirements.

title: Excessive volume
description: Sensor batches may contain more personal data than functionally needed for the exercise tracking functionality.

title: Treatment, analysis, enrichment
description: Data may be analyzed or enriched in ways not strictly necessary for the core functionality of the companion app.

title: Unawareness as data subject
description: Users may not be fully aware that their exercise data, GPS traces, and device ID are being collected and transferred.

title: Preferences
description: Users may lack control over preferences for how their personal data is processed or shared with the companion app.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (GPS traces, timestamps, device ID) may be processed than is actually needed for the core exercise tracking functionality.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking in the companion app.

title: Profiling of individual through calorie and weight data
description: The companion app can analyze calorie intake, meal patterns, and weight data to create profiles of the user's health and lifestyle patterns, potentially linking this data to other datasets.

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The system requests and processes identified personal data (calorie intake, meals, weight) which can be used to identify and profile the data subject.

title: Revealing attributes in health data
description: The data collected (calories, meals, weight) contains revealing attributes about the user's health status, dietary habits, and physical condition that support identification.

title: Sensitive health data collection
description: Calorie intake, meal patterns, and weight data are sensitive health-related data types that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for basic logging functionality.

title: Excessive volume of personal data
description: The volume of personal data (detailed calorie counts, meal entries, weight measurements) processed may exceed what is functionally needed for the companion app's basic logging purpose.

title: Unnecessary treatment and analysis of data
description: Personal data may be further treated, analyzed, and enriched in ways that are not necessary to achieve the basic functionality of the companion app.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: The data subject may not be fully aware of how their calorie, meal, and weight data is being collected, processed, stored, or disclosed by the companion app.

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: The data subject may lack control to set preferences or consent in how their personal health data is processed, stored, or shared.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (detailed calorie counts, meal entries, weight measurements) is processed than is actually needed for the basic functionality of the companion app.

title: Profiling of individuals through location pattern analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service analyzes location history data to derive daily routine and movement patterns, which constitutes profiling an individual based on their location data and user actions.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location history data contains revealing attributes that can support the identification of data subjects, such as home/work locations, movement patterns, and temporal information.

title: Unnecessary treatment and analysis of location data
description: Location history data is being analyzed and enriched to derive patterns, which may be more extensive than functionally required for the stated purpose of deriving daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Sensitive data type sensitivity
description: Location history data is a sensitive personal data type that should only be collected and processed when strictly required, as it can reveal intimate details about individuals' lives.

title: Unawareness of processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being queried and analyzed to derive daily routine and movement patterns, which could constitute unexpected processing of their personal data.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The processing of location history data may involve more personal data than is actually needed to achieve the functional goal of deriving daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Profiling of individuals through health analytics
description: The Health Analytics Service analyzes health data to create inferred insights (health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, trend flags) that can be used to profile individuals based on their health patterns and characteristics.

title: Revealing health attributes disclosed to app
description: Health-condition risk indicators and routine summaries contain revealing attributes that can support the identification of the data subject, as they provide specific health-related information about individuals.

title: Sensitive health data disclosed unnecessarily
description: Health data is highly sensitive and should only be disclosed when strictly required. The flow discloses health-condition risk indicators and trend flags that may be more sensitive than functionally required for the app's basic functionality.

title: Data propagation to app service
description: Personal data is propagated from the Health Analytics Service to the Companion Mobile App where it may be accessible beyond what is needed for the specific analytics function.

title: Data subject unawareness of analytics processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health data is being analyzed and that inferred insights are being generated and shared with their companion mobile app.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The analytics service may process and disclose more health-related personal data than is actually needed to achieve the functional goals of providing routine summaries and trend flags to the app.
